concepts.label: Audit Event
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - NOT reused as monitoring:event, despite superficial similarity ('a logged occurrence'). This page's audit_event has a fixed compliance-oriented schema (id/name/description/real_userid/local/remote/timestamp/sessionid), is written to a rotating per-node log FILE rather than a queryable/alertable stream, is categorized Admin/Data/User-Activity rather than by severity, and is never described as triggering anything. The promoted monitoring:event is explicitly 'scoped by... severity-enum' and 'subject of triggersAlert' - neither trait appears anywhere on this page, which never mentions Capella, monitoring, alerts, or severity at all. Minted separately; see this record's cross_product_finding for the full writeup.

concepts.label: Admin Event
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - subtype of audit:audit-event, tracking administrative/configuration changes

concepts.label: Data Event
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - subtype of audit:audit-event, sibling of audit:admin-event, tracking data access/change attempts

concepts.label: Audit User Activity
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - listed as the third audit-event type alongside Admin/Data events, but structurally different: it is a single mutable last-request timestamp per user, not an append-only stream of discrete event records - see doesNotSupport relation below

concepts.label: audit.log (rotating per-node audit log file)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - NOT reused as monitoring:activity-log, despite both being 'the log container for [administrative] actions'. This page's audit.log is an explicitly PER-NODE file (Each node captures its own events only... individual per node records must be manually consolidated by the administrator), rotated by time/size, with no cluster-wide aggregation described anywhere on this page. monitoring:activity-log was minted from Capella pages as 'the audit-log container for organization/project/cluster actions' - a cluster/org/project-scoped container, not a per-node file. Whether Capella's Activity Log is actually SURFACING this same per-node audit.log mechanism (Capella runs Couchbase Server underneath) or is a wholly separate management-plane audit trail cannot be determined from this page, which never mentions Capella. Minted separately per the no-silent-merge rule; flagged as the sharpest open question this batch found - see cross_product_finding.

notable_absence.finding: This page names three categories of audit event (Admin, Data, User Activity), shows six illustrative sample records (login success, login failure, bucket creation, bucket TTL modification, user creation, FTS index creation) to demonstrate field shape, and explicitly defers the complete flat list of individually-identified auditable events to a separate reference page, cited twice: 'See the reference page Audit Event Reference... for a complete list of events that can be audited.' That full flat list (which, going by the sample ids shown - 8192, 8193, 8201, 8202, 8232, 24577 - spans at least tens of distinct numbered event types) was deliberately NOT enumerated as one concept per event type/id here, per this round's brief. The six sample records were read only for their field-shape and category information (real_userid/local/remote/timestamp/roles/sessionid structure), not minted individually.

cross_component_finding: This page uses the word 'Eventing' generically to mean the emission of audit events ('Eventing for each cluster-node is disabled by default; and can be explicitly enabled') - a direct naming collision with Couchbase's Eventing Service (service:eventing-service, and the entire eventing:* namespace of promoted concepts: eventing:function, eventing:binding, eventing:timer, etc.), which is an unrelated JavaScript-handler compute service with nothing to do with auditing. The two uses of 'eventing' share no relationship whatsoever - flagged as a pure vocabulary collision for anyone doing keyword-based lookups against this ontology, not a modeling issue requiring any relation.
cross_product_finding: The single most important open question this batch was asked to help settle: is server's audit_event the same kind of thing as the promoted monitoring:event/monitoring:activity-log (both minted from Capella monitoring pages)? This page's own text does not state either way - it never mentions Capella, monitoring, alerts, or severity at all. But the STRUCTURE strongly suggests a different mechanism, not merely a different name for the same one: (1) monitoring:event is explicitly 'scoped by... severity-enum (Info/Warning/Critical)' and is 'subject of triggersAlert' - this page's audit_event has neither a severity field nor any alerting behavior anywhere in its field table or six sample records; (2) monitoring:activity-log is described as 'the audit-log container for organization/project/cluster actions' (an org/project/cluster-scoped container), while this page's audit.log is explicitly PER-NODE ('Each node captures its own events only... individual per node records must be manually consolidated by the administrator') with no cluster-wide view described; (3) this page categorizes events as Admin/Data/User-Activity, a taxonomy that shares no vocabulary with monitoring:event-severity-enum or monitoring:event-tag-enum. Called it: minted audit:audit-event and audit:audit-log as separate concepts from monitoring:event/monitoring:activity-log, not merged, not aliased. The genuinely open possibility - that Capella's Activity Log is a management-plane VIEW that surfaces this same underlying per-node audit.log mechanism, since Capella clusters run Couchbase Server underneath - is exactly the kind of relationship that would need a page stating it explicitly (a Capella auditing/activity-log page saying so, or a server/ page discussing Capella deployments) before it could be merged; no such page has been read in this round. Flagged as the batch's highest-value open question for reconciliation and, ultimately, SME review.
